title: Polarity Blindness in LLM Safety: A Systematic Study of Negation, Antonym Substitution, and Adversarial Framing
abstract: arXiv:2610.27908v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Negation remains a persistent challenge for language models across NLP tasks and modalities. We show that this weakness can undermine LLM safety guardrails through a structural vulnerability we term polarity blindness: the failure to recognize harmful intent after polarity-altering linguistic transformations. We study two forms of polarity inversion: grammatical negation and antonym replacement, and use synonym replacement as a polarity-preserving control. We further test whether an adversarial textual wrapper amplifies these failures. Using a 260-prompt benchmark across 10 state-of-the-art LLMs and 3 languages (English, Spanish, Czech), stratified by harmfulness potential and evaluated on a validated 0-5 harm scale, we find that polarity blindness affects most evaluated models, with mean harm scores reaching 4.12 for the most vulnerable model. translated_title: 大模型安全性中的极性盲视：对否定、反义词替换与对抗性框架的系统研究
translated_abstract: 否定一直是语言模型在各类NLP任务和模态中面临的持续性挑战。我们展示了这一弱点可以通过一种我们称之为“极性盲视”的结构性漏洞来削弱大模型的安全防护机制：即在极性改变的语言转换之后，模型无法识别有害意图。我们研究了两种极性反转的形式：语法否定和反义词替换，并使用同义词替换作为保持极性的对照组。我们进一步测试了对抗性文本包装是否会放大这些失效现象。我们使用了一个包含260个提示的基准测试，涵盖10个最先进的大语言模型和3种语言（英语、西班牙语、捷克语），按潜在危害性进行分层，并采用经过验证的0-5分危害量表进行评估。我们发现极性盲视影响了大多数被评估的模型，其中最脆弱模型的平均危害评分高达4.12。该效应在不同类型的否定系统中持续存在，表明极性盲视……
tldr: 大语言模型普遍存在“极性盲视”漏洞——在语法否定或反义词替换等极性改变的语言转换后无法识别有害意图，从而绕过安全防护，该漏洞在10个主流大模型和3种语言中均被验证，最脆弱模型的平均危害评分高达4.12。
en_tdlr: LLMs exhibit a structural vulnerability termed "polarity blindness"—failing to recognize harmful intent after polarity-altering transformations like negation and antonym substitution—affecting most of 10 state-of-the-art models across 3 languages, with the most vulnerable model reaching a mean harm score of 4.12.
